acceptanceCriteria: Mac reports directly observed verifier exit and original-group control separately from unproven escaped-descendant cleanup; no complete-tree claim.

Timeout, parent disconnect, output saturation, failed group or direct-child termination, and cleanup errors return after bounded observation. Record actual signal and kill results and whether the directly owned child was reaped; if exit or reaping is not confirmed by the deadline, persist cleanup Unknown rather than wait indefinitely or claim the process ended.

setsid, double-fork, closed-pipe, changed-cwd, stale owned-child handle, and controlled identity-loss negatives never become cleanup-success or reusable evidence; unrelated test-owned processes survive. Actual kernel PID reuse is not claimed as tested in this Work Item.
Cold read and restart retain Unknown; uncertainty cannot be promoted to clean by a later empty process-group probe.
Full composition supervision still rejects Mac before starting a verifier.
The nine scoped documents state HCI as the sole current North Star: understandable, controllable, explainable, recoverable; the historical map retains its historical identity.
A command's observed exit does not imply that arbitrary descendants were reaped or that governed verification passed.

A WI-local Summary records an actual process start with its execution and platform identity, then records confirmed direct-child reaping or explicit Unknown without erasing the history. A separate final cleanup command reads only that WI, skips already reaped entries, performs bounded cleanup only through a still-held and verified owner handle, and reports unowned live, zombie, missing, stale, or ambiguous entries as Unknown; it never signals an old numeric PID alone. Mac command results and cleanup assurance remain distinct, an Unknown attempt is not reusable or a formal pass, and finish/archive/close still require fresh formal verification in a capable environment. Supervisor death never implies handle transfer or cleanup.

A capable environment must perform fresh formal verification against its own Runtime, Contract, repository identity, and current source snapshot; the prior Mac attempt remains historical Unknown and is never promoted to clean.

The WI-local Summary lifecycle and independent final cleanup command use the same Rust-facing record and result semantics on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Platform-specific ownership and reaping mechanisms remain below that interface and may yield different proof strength; no platform claims cleanup solely from a stored PID, an empty group observation, or another platform's evidence. Normal verification does not require a cross-WI or always-running cleanup service.
goal: Use a common Rust execution record and a WI-local Summary to record each process actually started for this Work Item and whether its directly owned child was observed reaped. Provide a separate final process-cleanup command scoped to one WI: inspect those records, use only a still-held and verified process handle for bounded cleanup, and report Unknown when ownership, identity, or reaping cannot be proved. Keep ordinary verification usable, do not add a permanent service or cross-WI cleanup registry, and do not signal historical PID values alone. Preserve Mac's bounded direct-child/original-group limit and unsupported full composition supervision, honest Outcome, existing formal verification gates, and HCI as the sole North Star in English, Japanese, and Chinese.
